correctness.rationale: Euler additivity gives the exact/Frobenius subcategories; stalk or adjacent-stalk tests prove the ideal orthogonality; explicit cone constructions give complete ideal approximations for every subgroup B; long exact cohomology gives the necessary and sufficient truncation-Euler criteria and hence the sharp B=Z boundary.

originality.rationale: Qualified to the best of our knowledge. The current source treats only the parity case B=2Z. Directed searches did not locate the arbitrary Euler-subgroup theorem, zero-Euler case, or exact completeness boundary. Similar older Grothendieck-group restriction constructions remain a residual risk.

value.rationale: The result identifies the invariant behind the recent parity example, gives an infinite sharp family including a qualitatively distinct zero-Euler case, and classifies exactly when completeness descends from the ideal pair to its objects.

disclaimer: Not independent validation, peer review, formal verification, or a guarantee of first discovery.
